items.title: Section: Even a King May Only Give Away What Is Genuinely His — And His Own Family Only With Their Consent

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，若作國王，灌頂自在，統領方域。於自國界所有寮庶，終不抑奪取餘妻子而轉施餘。唯持村邑、聚落、川土，或全或分以用布施，
items.en: If bodhisattvas rule as king, anointed and sovereign over their realm, they never seize the spouse or children of any subject in their domain to give away to someone else. They give only towns, villages, or territory, whole or in part.

items.zh: 而告彼曰：如我恩化，汝亦宜然。
又諸菩薩，於自妻子、奴婢、僕使、親戚、眷屬，若不先以正言曉喻，令其歡喜，終不強逼令其憂惱施來求者。雖復先以正言曉喻，令其歡喜生樂欲心，而不施與怨家、惡友、藥叉、羅剎兇暴業者。不以妻子形容軟弱族姓男女，施來求者令作奴婢。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, regarding their own spouse, children, servants, or relatives, never coerce them into distress and give them to someone who asks unless they have first genuinely explained the matter and won their willing consent. ... Nor are they ever given to an enemy, a wicked companion, or a violently disposed being. Nor is a spouse or child of noble, gently-raised birth ever given away to become someone's servant.

items.title: Section: A Kingship Withheld From a Tyrant — Benefit to Others Concludes, Benefit to Oneself Opens

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，若有上品逼惱眾生樂行種種暴惡業者來求王位，終不施與。若彼暴惡補特伽羅先居王位，菩薩有力尚應廢黜，況當施與。
items.en: If someone who delights in oppressing beings through every kind of violent, unwholesome deed comes seeking kingship, bodhisattvas never grant it. If such a violent person already occupies the throne, a bodhisattva with the power to do so should even depose them — how much more so, then, never grant it to begin with.

items.title: Section: A New Angle Opens — Never Plundering One's Own Family, and a Mother Reborn as a Donkey

items.zh: 又諸菩薩終不侵奪父母、妻子、奴婢、僕使、親戚、眷屬所有財物，持用布施。亦不逼惱父母、妻子、奴婢、僕使、親戚、眷屬，以所施物施來求者。
items.en: Bodhisattvas never seize property belonging to their parents, spouse, servants, or relatives in order to give it away. Nor do they coerce their parents, spouse, servants, or relatives into distress in order to give what belongs to them to someone who asks.

items.title: Section: Wealth Honestly Gained, Precepts Never Broken, Equal Regard for Every Recipient

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，以其正法，以無卒暴積集財物而行惠施，不以非法、不以卒暴，亦不逼迫損惱於他而行惠施。又諸菩薩，若在諸佛聖教出家，終不違越所有學處而行惠施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas give using wealth gathered lawfully and without violence, never through unlawful means, violence, or by oppressing and harming others. Bodhisattvas who have gone forth in the Buddha's teaching never violate their precepts for the sake of giving.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩行布施時，普於一切有情之類起平等心，住福田想，而行惠施。終不分別怨親中庸、有德有失、劣等勝品、有苦有樂品類差別。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, when giving, give with a mind of equal regard towards every kind of being, regarding each as a field for planting merit, never distinguishing enemy from friend from stranger, the virtuous from the flawed, the lowly from the exalted, or the suffering from the joyful.

items.title: Giving Exactly as Promised — Never Shrunk, Never Downgraded

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，如先所說、如先所許，終無減少施來求者，唯有施彼或等、或增。又諸菩薩，終無先許勝妙財物，後施下劣；唯有先許下劣財物，若有勝妙後施勝妙。
items.en: Bodhisattvas never give less than what was previously stated or promised to someone who asks, only ever giving the same amount or more. Bodhisattvas never promise a fine object and then give something inferior; only, having promised something modest, may they later give something finer if it becomes available.

items.title: Section: Giving Free of Resentment, and Eight Faults That Silently Undo a Gift's Merit

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，不以異意、不以憤怒撓濁之心而行惠施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas do not give with a changed heart towards the recipient, nor with a mind disturbed and clouded by anger.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，終不施已而自稱讚，數數告言：我於汝所曾行如是如是惠施，攝受長養濟拔於汝。
items.en: Bodhisattvas never, after giving, praise themselves for it, repeatedly telling the recipient: I have done such-and-such generosity for you, gathering, nurturing, and rescuing you.

items.title: Section: Genuine Respect in Giving, and Never Growing Weary of a Difficult Recipient

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於卑賤者行布施時，尚無不敬撩擲而與，況於有德。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, giving even to the lowliest person, never carelessly toss the gift over without respect, let alone when giving to someone of genuine virtue.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，若來求者安住種種毀犯邪行、掉舉、躁擾，不自防護，專行罵詈、瞋忿、呵責，終不於彼暫起邪行帶厭倦心而行惠施。唯即於彼了知為諸煩惱所媚，令改本性，深更安住憐愍之心而行惠施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, if someone asking for a gift is caught up in undisciplined, agitated conduct, unguarded in speech, hurling abuse or anger or reproach, never respond to that person's momentary misconduct with a weary mind and give reluctantly. Rather, recognising them as simply led astray by affliction rather than their true nature, they abide all the more deeply in compassion and give.

items.title: Section: Giving Free of Superstition, and Not Mistaken for Liberation Itself

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，不由惡見妄有執取而行惠施，謂如廣大暴惡祠祀。不計殺生布施為法，亦不妄取吉祥瑞應相應相狀而行布施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas do not give while clinging to some distorted view — for instance, treating the killing done in some grand, violent sacrificial rite as though it were lawful conduct, nor wrongly insisting on auspicious signs or occasions before giving.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，終不妄計唯一切種極善清淨而行惠施，即是世間及出世間離欲清淨。唯審了知所行布施，但是離欲清淨資糧。
items.en: Bodhisattvas never wrongly assume that giving, however excellently and purely practised, is itself worldly or ultimate freedom from desire. They understand clearly that the giving they practise is only a provision supporting that freedom, not the freedom itself.

items.title: Section: Not Giving for a Reward, and the Four Ways a Gift's Fruit and Its Use Can Combine

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，不觀其果而行布施，一切布施皆為迴向速證無上正等菩提。
items.en: Bodhisattvas do not give while eyeing some resulting reward; all giving is dedicated towards swiftly realising unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，如實了知一切品類所行布施，一切品類施果異熟，深生信解，不由他緣、非他所引而行布施。謂施飲食能感大力，施諸衣服能感妙色，施諸車乘能感快樂，施諸燈明能感淨眼，如是等類廣說應知。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, truly understanding every kind of giving and the specific ripened fruit each kind produces, hold deep confidence in this, giving neither because led nor induced by anyone else. Giving food yields great strength; giving clothing yields fine appearance; giving a vehicle yields ease; giving lamps yields the pure, divine eye — and so on in detail, as should be understood.

items.title: Giving Free of the Fear of Poverty, and Never a Concealed or Improper Gift

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，不為怖畏自身貧窮而行布施，唯由悲愍眾生意樂而行布施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas do not give out of fear of their own future poverty, but purely from a heart of compassion for beings.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩於來求者，終不施與不合儀物。謂施出家者餘殘飲食，或諸便穢、洟唾、變吐、膿血，不淨所雜所染。又不告白不令覺知，如棄捨法施糜飯等。謂不食葱者，施以葱雜葱染飲食；不食肉者，施以肉雜肉染飲食；不飲酒者，施以酒雜酒染飲食。或復處置不合儀式所有事業而行布施。如是等類不合儀施，菩薩不為。
items.en: Bodhisattvas never give an improper object to someone who asks. ... Nor do they give without disclosure, concealing what is actually mixed into rice porridge or the like — giving onion-laced food to one who abstains from onion, meat-laced food to one who abstains from meat, or alcohol-laced food to one who abstains from alcohol. Nor do they place a recipient in circumstances genuinely unsuited to their calling while giving. None of this does a bodhisattva do.

blocks.text: More boundaries, then the positive qualities of right giving.

A king "never seizes the spouse or children of any subject to give away". One's own family and servants are never given against their will. One does not give kingship to a tyrant; if a violent person already rules, one tries to remove them. Venerable Miào Jìng explains the anointing of kings.
One never takes one's parents' or relatives' property to give it away. Master Cháng Bǎi tells a story about a son who beat a donkey that had been his mother.

"Wealth gathered lawfully and without violence." Monastic bodhisattvas never break precepts to give. "One gives with a mind of equal regard towards every being, regarding each as a field of merit, never distinguishing enemy from friend." Master Cháng Bǎi: giving to an ant in this spirit surpasses an offering to the Buddha given with discrimination.
Never giving less than promised, or something inferior to what was promised.

Not with "a changed heart" or "a mind clouded by anger"; never afterwards praising oneself: "I have done such generosity for you." Venerable Miào Jìng: a "changed heart" means one's feeling has changed.
"Even to the lowliest person, never carelessly tossing the gift." And never growing weary of a petitioner who is abusive or agitated: it is the affliction speaking.

Not treating ritual killing as lawful; not mistaking giving for liberation itself ("it is only a provision"); not giving "while eyeing some resulting reward"; not giving out of "fear of future poverty", but from compassion. And never giving improper things, or hiding what is mixed in, such as onion in food for one who abstains.

quiz.q: "If bodhisattvas rule as king, anointed and sovereign." How do the lectures explain "anointed"?
options: pouring water of the four great oceans over the head — the investiture as king
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: water from the four great oceans is poured over the head — that is the investiture, and he becomes king. Master Cháng Bǎi says the same.

quiz.q: The ellipsis omits "even though one has first explained rightly and won their glad consent." With it restored, what does "nor are they given to an enemy, a wicked companion, or a violent being" mean?
options: even if the family member has gladly consented, they are never given to enemies, wicked companions, or violent beings
with consent, anyone may receive them
quiz.why: The omitted clause means "even though one has explained and won their consent," so even with consent they are never given to violent beings. Master Cháng Bǎi: they may be given only with the person's own consent — consent is necessary but not sufficient.

quiz.q: Explaining "never seize property belonging to their parents … in order to give it away," what story does Master Cháng Bǎi tell?
options: someone stole four taels of silver from his father and was reborn as a donkey in that home to repay the debt ("whipping the donkey till it bleeds — who knows my mother's grief")
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi tells the story behind "whipping the donkey till it bleeds — who knows my mother's grief": because he stole four taels of silver from the father, he was reborn into that family to repay the debt.

quiz.q: With what kind of wealth do bodhisattvas give?
options: wealth gathered lawfully and without violence
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas give using wealth gathered lawfully and without violence, never through unlawful means, violence, or by oppressing and harming others." Venerable Miào Jìng: bodhisattvas too must acquire wealth lawfully.

quiz.q: "With a mind of equal regard towards every being, regarding each as a field of merit." When Master Cháng Bǎi says giving to an ant can surpass an offering to the Buddha, what is he stressing?
options: offering to the Buddha has no merit
do not make offerings to the Buddha
the power of a single moment of compassion — "mind superior, field inferior"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: giving to an ant with this frame of mind surpasses an offering to the Buddha — this stresses that single moment of compassion, "mind superior, field inferior." The reverse case is "field superior, mind inferior."

quiz.q: "Bodhisattvas never, after giving, praise themselves for it." How do the two lectures explain this?
options: both: fine as long as it's not said to the recipient
Cháng Bǎi cites the eight faults in the 《大集經》: praising oneself after giving drains the merit; Miào Jìng: the bodhisattva never brings it up again
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi lists, as the fourth of eight faults, praising oneself after giving to the recipient and others, which drains away the merit. Venerable Miào Jìng: bodhisattvas do not say such things — what happened before, they never bring up again.

quiz.q: "They understand clearly that the giving they practise is only a provision supporting freedom from desire." How do the two lectures relate giving to that freedom?
options: both agree: giving is a cause and a provision, not to be mistaken for the result; Cháng Bǎi adds that worldly freedom from desire is attaining meditative absorption, and world-transcending freedom is attaining the noble path
Miào Jìng: giving is the result; Cháng Bǎi: giving is an obstacle
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: worldly freedom from desire is attaining meditative absorption; world-transcending freedom is attaining the noble path — do not mistake the cause for the result. Venerable Miào Jìng: giving is by nature a provision, a cause for obtaining the result, a preliminary means.
